answer_1.quote: Our goal is not to silence the LLM on sensitive topics, but to equip it with the means to modify language at a stylistic level... We propose a holistic framework for implicit knowledge editing to achieve this, with the aim of making LLMs more "politically correct"... The proposed framework is evaluated in a toxicity removal setup... The evaluation comprises conditional text generation where the model continues a toxic prompt.
answer_1.outputs: detoxified continuations or paraphrases of input sentences

answer_2.quote: We assess the semantic similarity of the input context and the output sequence using the cosine similarity of the embeddings... Toxicity is assessed with HateBERT... Diversity is measured using dist-n scores... Fluency is evaluated via perplexity (PPL) on WikiText2.

answer_3.quote: We conducted experiments in an "LLM-as-judge" setup on the generated output... we used an uncensored Qwen-2.5-7b. The proposed approach is the favored model with a significant margin of (+9.0%) compared to the second-best model...
